operations.specification: Implement customer account registration by validating the submitted email and password payload, ensuring the email is not already registered, creating the customer account record, and initializing the authentication session response in a single transaction. The service should also trigger any required account-verification or security side effects that are supported by the customer authentication workflow, such as issuing verification-related records when the platform requires email confirmation. Return a standardized authorized response containing access and refresh tokens or equivalent authorization payload after successful creation.
operations.description:
Create a new customer account using the registration credentials defined for the shopping mall platform.

This operation is the entry point for a registered shopper identity and is aligned with the customer actor described in the system requirements. It is responsible for creating the account that will later participate in profile management, shipping addresses, wishlist, cart, orders, and reviews. The operation must respect the customer account security model, which centers on email-and-password credentials and the account security state stored for customer actors.

The registration flow must validate that the submitted email is unique and that the password satisfies the platform’s security requirements. After successful creation, the service should return an authorization payload that allows the newly created customer to continue into authenticated flows. If the platform’s customer verification flow is enabled by the underlying schema, the registration process should also integrate with the email-verification support tables used by customer authentication.

This endpoint is part of the required authentication trio for the customer actor and is distinct from all business CRUD operations. It must not expose profile, order, or wishlist functionality. Related follow-up operations include customer login for returning users and token refresh for renewing an active session.

requestBody.description: Customer registration credentials for creating a new shopper account.

responseBody.description: Authorization result returned after a successful customer registration.

operations.name: join

operations.specification: Implement customer login by validating the submitted email and password against the customer credential store, rejecting banned or otherwise disabled accounts, and creating or updating the customer session state as appropriate for JWT-based authentication. The service should issue an access token and a refresh token, persist session-tracking data when the schema supports it, and ensure that login failure cases do not leak whether the email exists beyond standard authentication error handling.
operations.description:
Authenticate an existing customer using the email-and-password account credentials defined for the shopping mall platform.

This operation is used by a registered shopper who already has an account and needs to regain authenticated access to customer-only features such as address management, cart checkout, order history, and review management. The customer actor is a member actor, so login is a required authentication operation and must be available alongside registration and token refresh.

The login process must verify the provided credentials against the customer account records and respect the account security state stored for customers. If the account is not permitted to log in, the operation must fail with an authentication error. When successful, the response should return the platform’s authorized payload so the client can proceed with authenticated requests.

This endpoint should be treated as a pure authentication boundary and should not be mixed with business actions like profile editing or order operations. It is designed to work together with customer session storage and token refresh flows, allowing the client to continue a secure session without re-entering credentials each time.

requestBody.description: Customer login credentials used to authenticate an existing shopper account.

responseBody.description: Authorization result returned after successful customer credential validation.

operations.name: login

operations.specification: Implement customer token refresh by validating the provided refresh-token payload, verifying that the token matches an active customer session when session tracking is supported, and issuing a new authorized token set. The service must reject expired, revoked, or mismatched refresh credentials and should rotate or update stored session state according to the platform’s JWT session policy. This operation should not create a new account or re-check passwords; it exists solely to renew authentication for an already signed-in customer.
operations.description:
Renew a customer’s authenticated session using the refresh credentials issued by the platform.

This operation supports the customer actor’s JWT-based authentication lifecycle and is required so that a signed-in shopper can continue using authenticated features without re-entering their email and password. The platform’s customer session support, including the dedicated customer session table and related account security structures, makes token renewal a first-class authentication operation.

The refresh flow must verify that the submitted refresh token is still valid and associated with the customer session state. If the token is expired, revoked, or otherwise invalid, the request must be rejected. On success, the response must provide a fresh authorized payload so the client can continue calling protected customer endpoints such as cart checkout, address management, order history, and review actions.

This endpoint is intentionally limited to authentication renewal. It does not expose any business data and should be used together with login and registration as part of the customer’s full authentication lifecycle.

requestBody.description: Customer refresh-token payload used to renew an active authenticated session.

responseBody.description: Authorization result returned after successful customer token refresh.

operations.name: refresh

operations.specification: Implement a seller registration endpoint that creates a new seller account identity using the submitted email and password credentials, then returns authorized tokens after the account is successfully created. The service should validate the registration payload, ensure the email is unique among seller accounts, and persist the new seller record in the sellers actor table. If the platform requires seller approval before selling, the registration flow must still create the account but leave any approval-related state in the pending/default state defined by the seller account lifecycle. After persistence, issue access and refresh tokens tied to the newly created seller session record so the seller can continue to authenticated onboarding flows immediately.
operations.description:
Create a new seller account for a merchant who wants to join the marketplace as a registered seller. This endpoint is the first authentication step for the seller actor and is used when a merchant submits email and password credentials to establish a seller identity in the system.

The seller account model supports account credentials and lifecycle state, so this operation must create the account record and initialize it in a valid pre-selling state consistent with the seller approval workflow. The response returns authorization data so the seller can proceed with authenticated onboarding and account management after successful registration.

This operation is only for seller account creation and must not be confused with profile editing, seller approval review, or account suspension management. Those are separate business operations and are not part of the authentication flow. The request must be validated carefully because seller registration is the entry point for the seller actor's authenticated session lifecycle.

requestBody.description: Seller registration credentials for creating a new seller account.

responseBody.description: Authorized seller session tokens returned after successful registration.

operations.name: join

operations.specification: Implement a seller login endpoint that verifies the submitted seller email and password against the stored seller credentials, then creates or renews a seller session and returns authorization tokens. The service should locate the seller account by email, confirm the password using the stored credential hash, and reject the request if the account is banned, otherwise unavailable, or fails any seller account security checks defined by the platform. On success, generate a fresh access token and refresh token pair and store the session tracking data in the seller sessions table so the authentication state can be managed consistently.
operations.description:
Authenticate an existing seller account using email and password credentials. This endpoint is the primary sign-in operation for merchants who already have a registered seller identity and need a valid session to access seller-specific features such as product management, inventory control, shipment handling, cancellation responses, and refund responses.

The seller actor is a member-level account type, so login is required after registration to obtain a valid authenticated session. The seller account schema supports credential-based access and session tracking, which makes this endpoint the correct place to validate credentials and issue authorization tokens for subsequent requests.

This endpoint must reject invalid credentials and any seller account state that prevents login according to the account security rules. It is separate from seller approval review and separate from profile or storefront management operations.

requestBody.description: Seller login credentials used to authenticate an existing seller account.

responseBody.description: Authorized seller session tokens returned after successful login.

operations.name: login

operations.specification: Implement a seller token refresh endpoint that accepts the seller refresh payload, validates the current refresh token or session reference, and issues a new authorized token pair. The service should verify that the seller session exists, has not been revoked, and is still valid before rotating or reusing the refresh token according to the platform's session policy. If validation succeeds, return a new access token and refresh token pair and update the seller session tracking record to reflect the renewed authentication state.
operations.description:
Renew an authenticated seller session by exchanging a valid refresh credential for a new authorization result. This endpoint exists so a seller can continue working without re-entering email and password while their current access token expires over time.

The seller session model supports refresh tracking and revocation control, which makes this endpoint essential for maintaining secure long-lived seller authentication. The response provides fresh authorization data that can be used for continued access to seller-only functions such as product editing, inventory adjustments, shipment processing, and request handling.

This endpoint is not a login endpoint and must not create a brand-new account. It only extends an already authenticated seller session and should fail if the refresh token or session state is invalid, revoked, or expired.

requestBody.description: Seller refresh credentials used to renew an existing authenticated session.

responseBody.description: Authorized seller session tokens returned after successful refresh.

operations.name: refresh

operations.specification:
Implement administrator self-registration by validating the submitted credentials, creating a new administrator account record, and issuing JWT access and refresh tokens on success. The service must enforce uniqueness of the administrator email, hash the password before persistence, initialize the account security state in the administrator table, and create an administrator session record so the refresh token can be tracked and revoked later.

The handler should run inside a transaction that inserts the administrator row and the corresponding session row atomically. If the email is already registered, the operation must fail with a conflict-style error. The response should contain the authorized token payload in the standardized IShoppingMallAdministrator.IAuthorized DTO.
operations.description:
Creates a new administrator account and immediately returns authorization tokens for the newly registered administrator.

This operation is the entry point for administrator account onboarding in the platform. It corresponds to the administrator account model stored in the administrator table, which represents registered administrator accounts with email and password credentials, role grade, and account security state. The registration flow must persist a secure account record and establish a session so the administrator can continue using privileged management features without a separate login step after successful join.

The registration payload is validated against the administrator account constraints before any record is created. Email uniqueness must be enforced, password values must be processed securely, and the created account must be associated with the platform's administrator session tracking model so that the issued refresh token can later be renewed or revoked. This operation is part of the required administrator authentication workflow and is separate from moderation or management permissions granted after authentication.

Because administrators are privileged actors, the generated account must still respect the same security boundaries used throughout the platform: account credentials are stored securely, and the session token lifecycle is tracked by the administrator session store. If the submitted email is already in use, the request must be rejected and no session should be created.

This endpoint is typically used together with administrator login and token refresh. After join succeeds, the client receives authorization tokens and can continue using administrator-only endpoints without additional onboarding steps.

requestBody.description: Administrator registration credentials and account setup data.

responseBody.description: Authorized administrator token payload returned after successful registration.

operations.name: join

operations.specification:
Validate administrator email and password credentials, verify that the account is active and eligible for login, then issue fresh JWT access and refresh tokens. The implementation must compare the submitted password against the stored password hash in the administrator account record, reject invalid credentials, and create or update the administrator session tracking record for the new token pair.

This operation should be stateless from the client's perspective but stateful in the session store for refresh token management and revocation support. On successful authentication, the service returns the standardized authorized DTO. Invalid credentials, banned or otherwise ineligible accounts, and inactive administrator states must all be rejected without leaking sensitive account details.
operations.description:
Authenticates an existing administrator using email and password credentials and returns authorization tokens for the session.

This operation is the primary credential validation step for the administrator actor. It works with the registered administrator account model, which stores the email/password account identity, role grade, and security state, and it participates in the administrator session lifecycle by issuing the session tokens tracked in the administrator session store. The login flow is required because administrators are authenticated actors who perform privileged platform tasks such as seller approval review, category management, user moderation, product oversight, and order oversight.

The request is validated against the stored administrator account data. The submitted email must match a registered administrator account, the submitted password must match the stored password hash, and the account must be in a state that permits login. The session store is then used to persist the refresh token metadata so that token renewal and revocation can be managed consistently with the platform's security model.

This endpoint is tightly coupled with administrator join and administrator refresh. It is the normal authentication path when an administrator already has an account, and it should return the same standardized authorization payload used by the other administrator auth endpoints. Failed authentication must not reveal whether the email exists or which credential check failed.

requestBody.description: Administrator login credentials used to authenticate an existing account.

responseBody.description: Authorized administrator token payload returned after successful login.

operations.name: login

operations.specification:
Accept a valid administrator refresh token, verify it against the stored administrator session record, ensure the session is still active, and issue a new token pair. The implementation must check the refresh token integrity, locate the associated administrator session, and reject revoked, expired, or unknown sessions. When rotation is used, the service should replace the stored refresh token value and update the session record atomically.

The refresh endpoint exists to renew authentication without forcing the administrator to resubmit email and password. It depends on the administrator session tracking model so that long-lived access can be controlled and revoked properly. The response must return the standardized authorized token payload after successful renewal.
operations.description:
Renews an authenticated administrator session by exchanging a valid refresh token for a new authorized token payload.

This operation is part of the administrator session lifecycle. It uses the administrator session table, which stores JWT session tokens for administrator login sessions, including refresh token tracking and revocation support. The refresh flow allows an already authenticated administrator to continue accessing privileged platform functions without re-entering credentials, while still preserving the ability to detect revoked or expired sessions.

The submitted refresh request is validated against the active administrator session record. The token must correspond to a known session, must not be revoked, and must remain within its valid lifetime. If the session is no longer valid, the request must fail and no new tokens should be issued. When the refresh succeeds, the session record should be updated consistently so that the refreshed token pair is the only valid continuation of that login session.

This endpoint is used together with administrator login and administrator join. It is the normal follow-up when an access token expires and the client needs to continue operating as an administrator without a full sign-in flow.

requestBody.description: Administrator refresh token payload used to renew an active session.

responseBody.description: Authorized administrator token payload returned after successful refresh.

operations.name: refresh

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of customer accounts for platform browsing and administration.

This operation returns customer account records in summary form so that authorized users can inspect the registered shopper population, review account status, and support operational oversight. It is aligned with the platform rule that customers must be registered before they can use customer-facing features, so the collection represents registered customer identities rather than anonymous visitors.

The response is intentionally summary-oriented and should not expose credential data. It is designed for list views, management screens, and account review workflows where the caller needs searchable, filterable access to customer accounts. Pagination is required so the platform can handle large customer populations efficiently while preserving consistent browsing behavior.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Implement a paginated customer account search over the shopping_mall_customers table.

Use request-body criteria to support filtering, sorting, and pagination in a single query. Return a page container of customer summaries rather than full account records so that sensitive fields such as password credentials are never exposed.

Service behavior:
- Query the customers table with optional filters for account status, email keyword, and registration-related browsing fields if supported by the schema.
- Apply deterministic sorting, with a default newest-first order if the request does not specify otherwise.
- Enforce pagination limits and normalize invalid page parameters to service defaults.
- Join or enrich results only when needed for list display; do not load unrelated profile, session, or password reset data.
- If the platform supports administrator/customer visibility constraints, apply them here so callers only receive permitted customer records.

Validation and error handling:
- Reject malformed pagination or sort requests with validation errors.
- Return an empty page when no records match the search criteria.
- Do not include deleted-account handling logic unless the schema explicitly provides a corresponding field; this endpoint must rely only on actual stored customer state.

Response shaping:
- Map records to a summary DTO suitable for list browsing.
- Include pagination metadata in the page wrapper.
- Keep the payload stable and minimal for efficient admin browsing.

responseBody.description: Paginated customer account summaries

requestBody.description: Search, filtering, sorting, and pagination criteria for customer browsing

operations.description:
Retrieve a single customer account and its associated profile information.

This endpoint returns the registered customer identity record together with the public-facing profile data that belongs to that account. The customer record is the canonical identity for the shopper, storing the email address, account status, and account lifecycle timestamps. The linked profile record contains the display name and phone number used as the customer’s account-facing identity across shopping features.

The response is intended for the owning customer and for administrators who need to inspect a customer account for support, moderation, or account-management purposes. A caller must be authorized to view the requested account; a customer may only read their own record, while administrators may read any customer record. If the customer account has been deleted and the profile has been removed, the API should reflect the current persisted account state and omit unavailable profile data when there is no profile record.

Use this operation when the UI needs to preload account identity data before profile editing, account review, or administrative inspection. It complements the profile update operations, which change the display name and phone number stored in the customer profile table. The endpoint does not create, update, or delete data, and it does not expose authentication credentials such as the password hash.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Load the customer row by primary key from shopping_mall_customers and left-join the one-to-one shopping_mall_customer_profiles relation using shopping_mall_customer_profiles.shopping_mall_customer_id.

Validate the path parameter as a UUID and fetch the target account in a read-only query. If the authenticated actor is a customer, require that the authenticated customer ID matches customerId. If the authenticated actor is an administrator, allow access to any customer account. Return a not-found or forbidden response according to the platform’s authorization policy when the target cannot be accessed.

Select only business-safe fields: customer id, email, account_status, banned_at, deleted_at, created_at, updated_at, and the nested profile fields display_name, phone_number, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at when the profile exists. Never expose password_hash.

If the profile relation is absent, return the customer record with a null profile reference or an equivalent absent nested object in the generated schema. Because this is a pure retrieval endpoint, no transaction beyond a standard read is required. Ensure the response model is a single resource schema, not a page schema.

responseBody.description: Customer account details with profile information.

operations.description:
Update the authenticated customer's profile information.

This operation lets a customer change the public-facing profile data stored in the customer profile record, which is limited to the display name and phone number. The customer profile is the human-readable part of the account identity used in customer-facing contexts and is separate from login credentials. Because this profile belongs to exactly one customer account, the server resolves the target profile from the authenticated session rather than from a path parameter.

Only the owner of the profile may call this endpoint. The platform must reject the request when the account is not registered, not active, or has been deleted. When the profile is updated, the previous profile state must be preserved in snapshot history so the system can support dispute review and audit needs for money-related commerce workflows.

This operation does not modify seller profile information, login credentials, shipping addresses, or any other customer data. It is intended only for updating the customer-owned display name and phone number shown in account and checkout-related customer-facing views.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Authenticate the caller as a customer and load the current customer's profile through the one-to-one customer relationship. Verify that the account is registered, active, and not deleted before allowing any change.

Validate the request body so that only display_name and phone_number are accepted and both are persisted as the customer profile's editable values. Reject any attempt to update identity keys, ownership fields, timestamps, or non-profile data. Apply any field-level validation defined by the profile domain rules before saving.

Before persisting the new values, create a profile snapshot containing the prior state so the change history remains available for audit and dispute resolution. Then update the existing shopping_mall_customer_profiles row inside a single transaction. Return the updated profile after commit.

If the profile record cannot be found for the authenticated customer, or if the account is inactive or deleted, return an authorization/validation failure rather than creating a new profile. Keep the operation strictly customer-scoped; do not permit admin-style cross-account edits through this endpoint.

responseBody.description: The updated customer profile.

requestBody.description: Customer profile fields to update.

operations.description:
Complete an email verification using the submitted verification token.

This endpoint finalizes the email ownership confirmation flow for both customer and seller accounts. The platform stores verification attempts in dedicated verification records that contain the token, the timestamp when the verification email was issued, the expiration time, and the timestamp when verification was completed. When a valid token is submitted, the matching verification record is marked as verified and the verification completion time is recorded.

The endpoint is part of the account onboarding and email revalidation flow, so it must be callable before the user is fully active in the application. It must not expose whether a token belongs to a customer account or a seller account in the public response. The server should resolve the token against the customer verification table and the seller verification table, then apply the verification update only to the record that matches and is still valid.

Verification must fail when the token is unknown, expired, or already used. The implementation should preserve the original issued-at and expiration information so the verification history remains auditable. Because the verification tables are designed to keep the verification lifecycle separate from the account identity records, this endpoint should only update the verification record state and delegate any account activation follow-up to the account management layer if needed.
operations.name: validate
operations.specification:
Accept a verification token in the request body and search for a matching record in the customer email verification table and the seller email verification table.

Perform the lookup by token and ensure the record has not already been verified and has not expired. If the token matches a customer verification record, update verified_at to the current timestamp in a transaction that preserves the original sent_at and expired_at values. If the token matches a seller verification record, perform the same update on that record. If a matching record exists in both tables due to data inconsistency, the service should reject the request and surface a server-side integrity error rather than verifying both.

Use a single transactional boundary for lookup and update so concurrent verification attempts cannot double-apply the completion. Return a success response that does not reveal which actor type was verified. If the token is invalid, expired, or already verified, return a validation-style failure that allows the client to show a generic verification error message.

Do not create new verification records here. Do not delete verification records here. Do not attempt account login or session creation as part of this endpoint. The only state change in scope is marking the matching verification record as completed.

responseBody.description: Email verification result.

requestBody.description: Verification token used to confirm email ownership.

operations.description:
Retrieve a single email verification record by its identifier.

This operation returns the current state of one verification attempt used for account registration confirmation or email ownership validation. The underlying verification records store the owning account reference, the unique token, the time the verification email was issued, the optional time verification completed, and the time the token expires. These fields allow clients and support tools to understand whether the verification is still valid, already completed, or no longer usable.

The record belongs to either a customer account or a seller account depending on which verification table it was created from. The customer verification record stores the issuance time alongside the token lifecycle, while the seller verification record stores the expiration and completion state for seller onboarding and re-verification. Access to this endpoint should be limited to the owning authenticated account or an administrator, because verification records expose security-sensitive lifecycle information tied to account access and registration flows.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Load the email verification record by its UUID primary key. The implementation should search the customer verification table and the seller verification table according to the platform's email verification routing rules, then return the matching record as a single detail response.

Validate that the path parameter is a UUID. If no record exists, return a not-found response. If the record exists but is associated with a different account, reject access unless the requester is an administrator. Do not expose or transform the token beyond the persisted value required by the response schema.

The operation is read-only and must not modify verified_at, expired_at, created_at, or updated_at. It should rely on the verification tables' existing indexes on token and account/timestamp combinations for efficient lookup logic where applicable, and it should preserve the distinction between customer and seller verification ownership when composing the final response.

responseBody.description: Email verification details.

operations.description:
Change the password for a customer, seller, or administrator account after verifying ownership or a valid reset token.

This operation updates the login credentials stored in the corresponding account table while keeping the account itself active. It is used for account-owner password changes and secure password recovery flows, and it relies on the matching password reset record to validate that the requester is authorized to replace the current password.

For customers, the operation works with the customer account identity in shopping_mall_customers and the token lifecycle in shopping_mall_customer_password_resets. For sellers, it uses shopping_mall_sellers and shopping_mall_seller_password_resets. For administrators, it uses shopping_mall_administrators and shopping_mall_administrator_password_resets. In each case, the reset token record contains the secret token, expiration time, and consumption timestamp used to enforce one-time use and prevent reuse of an expired or already consumed credential-reset request.

The password change must only succeed when the current account owner is authorized or the presented reset token is still valid, unexpired, and unused. After a successful change, the platform stores the new password hash on the account record, records the token as consumed, and returns the updated account identity so the caller can continue using the account with the new credentials.

This endpoint is part of the account security lifecycle and should be used together with sign-in flows and any password reset request issuance flow. It does not modify profile data, session data, approval status, or account status, because those concerns belong to separate account-management operations.
operations.name: process
operations.specification:
Implement a credential-change workflow that supports three account families: customer, seller, and administrator.

1. Determine the target account type from the request body and load the matching account record and reset-token record.
2. Verify the request is authorized either by the authenticated account owner or by a valid password-reset token tied to the same account.
3. Reject the request if the token is missing, expired, already used, mismatched, or if the current password verification fails.
4. Hash the new password using the platform password hashing policy and update only the password_hash field on the target account table.
5. Mark the matching reset-token row as used by setting used_at, and leave the rest of the account state unchanged.
6. Use a transaction so the password update and token consumption succeed or fail together.
7. Return the updated account identity summary for the target actor type.
8. Emit an authorization failure for ownership mismatch, and a validation failure for weak password input or malformed reset payload.

Do not update email, account_status, approval_status, banned_at, suspended_at, or profile-related fields. Do not create any new account records. Keep the operation idempotent with respect to token reuse by rejecting already-consumed reset tokens instead of processing them again.

responseBody.description: Updated account identity after the password change completes.

requestBody.description: Password reset credentials and target account information.

operations.description:
Retrieve a single password reset record by its identifier.

This operation returns the current state of one password reset token record, including the owning account reference, the reset token value, the expiration time, and whether the token has already been consumed. The underlying database models describe password reset tables as dedicated support entities for account recovery and password change flows, so this endpoint is intended to expose that token lifecycle state without modifying any data.

The returned record reflects the security status of the reset request at the moment of retrieval. Clients can use it to determine whether the token is still valid, already used, or expired. The endpoint does not create a new reset token, does not mark the token as used, and does not update the associated account credentials; those behaviors belong to separate account recovery or password change flows.

Because password reset records are stored in separate tables for customers, sellers, and administrators, the service implementation should resolve the requested identifier against the appropriate reset record source used by the current recovery flow. Access to this endpoint should be restricted to authorized account recovery or support workflows, since the response contains sensitive token-state information tied to an account credential reset process.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Load the password reset record by primary key from the password reset repository used by the active recovery flow. The implementation should treat this as a pure read operation: no token consumption, no expiration update, no audit mutation beyond normal read handling.

Validate that passwordResetId is a UUID path parameter. Query the backing password reset table for the matching record and return 404 when not found. If the record is logically unavailable for the current flow because it is expired or already used, still return the record data so the caller can inspect the state; do not change the stored state in this endpoint.

Because the system has separate password reset tables for customer, seller, and administrator accounts, the implementation should route to the correct repository/context based on the current password reset domain. If the architecture exposes a unified façade, it should resolve the resource to one concrete record source and map the fields directly. Do not include any request body or list pagination. Preserve sensitive token data handling according to the platform’s security layer and logging policy.

responseBody.description: Password reset record details.

operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of the authenticated account’s sessions.

This operation exposes the login sessions that belong to the currently signed-in customer, seller, or administrator account. Each session record represents one authentication event and includes connection context such as the originating IP address, the entry URL, the referrer URL, and the creation and expiration timestamps stored in the corresponding session table.

The returned data is intended for security review and session management. It allows the current account holder to inspect where and when sessions were created, while platform rules ensure that banned or otherwise inactive accounts cannot continue using sessions to access protected functionality. The operation must always respect the caller’s actor boundary: customer sessions are read from the customer session store, seller sessions from the seller session store, and administrator sessions from the administrator session store.

Because a single account may have many sessions over time, the response is paginated and supports filtering and sorting. The service should only return sessions that belong to the authenticated account and remain valid under the account’s current status. Expired sessions should be excluded from active-session views unless the request explicitly asks for historical inspection.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Resolve the authenticated principal and determine whether the caller is a customer, seller, or administrator. Reject the request if the account is banned or otherwise prevented from using platform sessions according to the current account status.

Query the corresponding session table for the principal type: shopping_mall_customer_sessions, shopping_mall_seller_sessions, or shopping_mall_administrator_sessions. Scope the query strictly by the authenticated account id; never allow cross-account session access. Apply pagination and optional sorting by created_at descending by default so the newest sessions appear first. If the request body supports historical inspection, include expired_at filtering options, but keep the default behavior focused on currently valid sessions.

Return a paginated summary DTO with session identifiers and connection metadata suitable for a session management UI. Do not expose password hashes or other account credentials. Do not mutate session records in this operation. If the account status check fails, return an authorization or access-state error before any session lookup. If the session set is empty, return an empty page rather than an error.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of session summaries for the authenticated account.

requestBody.description: Search, pagination, and sorting criteria for the current account's sessions.

operations.description:
Retrieve a single authenticated session by its identifier.

This operation returns the session metadata recorded when the user signed in, including the owning account reference, the IP address used at creation time, the request URL or entry context, the referrer URL, the creation timestamp, and the expiration timestamp. The session record is a security-focused authentication artifact and is not business data, so it is used for session inspection, account security screens, and validation of whether the current access token is still valid.

The returned session belongs to exactly one account of the same actor type that created it. A customer session is owned by a customer account, a seller session is owned by a seller account, and an administrator session is owned by an administrator account. Access to this endpoint must remain within the authenticated actor boundary, and the request should be rejected if the caller attempts to inspect a session outside their own account scope unless they have privileged administrative oversight rights.

The session is only meaningful while the owning account remains active. If the owning account is banned, deleted, suspended, or otherwise loses access according to its account status, the session should no longer be considered usable for authenticated features. This endpoint supports that lifecycle by allowing the application to inspect the stored expiration and ownership details before continuing an authenticated flow.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Load the session record by primary key from the appropriate session table based on the authenticated actor type. Resolve the runtime actor context first, then query the matching session repository: customer sessions for customers, seller sessions for sellers, administrator sessions for administrators. Do not attempt cross-table lookup without actor context because each session table stores only its own actor type.

Validate that the requested session belongs to the authenticated principal unless the caller has explicit administrative privilege for security review. If the record exists but belongs to a different account, return a forbidden/unauthorized error. If the record does not exist, return not found. If the owning account is banned, deleted, or otherwise inactive according to account lifecycle rules, still return the record only when the caller is the owner or an authorized administrator, but ensure downstream session validation treats it as unusable.

Use a single read query and do not mutate any state. The response should include id, owner account id, ip, href, referrer, createdAt, and expiredAt. No transaction is necessary because this is a pure read, but the service should still perform consistent authorization checks before serializing the result. If the implementation later introduces a unified session abstraction, map the session-specific table row into that shared response model without exposing any additional hidden fields.

responseBody.description: The requested session record.

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of seller accounts for browsing and management.

This endpoint returns seller records as a searchable collection that supports platform administration and storefront discovery. A seller is the registered merchant identity in the marketplace, and each seller may expose a public-facing shop identity through the seller profile, including the shop name, shop description, and logo image used in customer-facing views.

The response is intended for list views, so it should provide summary-level seller information rather than full security-sensitive account details. The operation should support pagination, keyword search, and sorting so administrators can efficiently review sellers and so any permitted browsing screen can present a stable, filtered directory. It must not expose password credentials, session tokens, or password reset data.

This operation should align with seller lifecycle and approval management rules. Seller accounts may exist in states such as pending review, approved, or rejected, and the list should allow the caller to filter by account or approval status when needed. The seller profile is a separate business concept that represents shop identity; when available, its fields should be included in the summary so the list can show shop name and branding information alongside the seller account.

Clients should use this endpoint before navigating to seller-specific detail or administrative review flows. For example, a management screen may use this collection to find sellers by name or status, then load a single seller detail endpoint for a full record. Invalid pagination, search, or sort inputs should be rejected with a clear validation error, and the response must remain stable even when individual sellers have incomplete optional profile data.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Implement a paginated seller directory query over shopping_mall_sellers with optional joins to shopping_mall_seller_profiles for public shop identity fields.

Accept a request body for search, pagination, and sorting. Validate page, pageSize, query string, and allowed filter values. Support filtering by approval/account status and keyword matching against seller identity fields and seller profile shop name. If the list is used by administrators, ensure the service can also filter by moderation state without exposing restricted security columns.

Build the response as a paginated summary list. Each row should include the seller identifier, account status/approval state, and summary shop profile information when present. Do not include password hashes, session data, email verification tokens, or password reset records. If seller profile data is missing, return the seller record with null or absent profile summary fields according to the summary schema.

Use a deterministic sort order, defaulting to newest or most recently created seller records if such a column exists in the schema; otherwise sort by stable identifier order. Apply count query and data query in the same filtering scope so pagination metadata matches the returned rows. Handle empty results gracefully.

This is a read-only list operation, so no transaction is needed unless the implementation performs a consistent count/data query wrapper. Return validation errors for malformed pagination, disallowed filters, or unsupported sort keys. Authorization should allow administrator access and any other role explicitly permitted by the business rules for seller browsing, but never expose sensitive auth/session fields.

responseBody.description: Paginated seller summaries

requestBody.description: Search, filter, pagination, and sorting criteria for sellers

operations.description:
Retrieve a single seller account by its unique identifier.

This operation returns the canonical seller identity record used by the marketplace for merchant-facing access control, approval workflow visibility, and administrative oversight. The seller account includes the login email, current approval status, rejection reason when present, account security state, and the timestamps that describe approval, rejection, suspension, ban, and last successful login activity.

The response reflects the current state stored in the shopping_mall_sellers table. It is intended for the seller who owns the account and for administrators who need to inspect seller accounts during moderation, support, or enforcement workflows. The seller account must be treated as an account-level resource, not as a storefront profile resource; shop identity details are managed separately in seller profile data.

This endpoint returns one seller record only. It should reject requests for nonexistent identifiers and should never expose the password hash field. Clients that need seller approval review context can use this operation together with seller approval request operations, while storefront presentation data should be retrieved through seller profile endpoints.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Load one row from shopping_mall_sellers by primary key id.
Verify that the authenticated actor is either the seller owner for that id or an administrator. Sellers may access only their own account record; administrators may access any seller record.

Select all public seller account columns except password_hash. Include id, email, approval_status, rejection_reason, account_status, approved_at, rejected_at, suspended_at, banned_at, last_login_at, created_at, updated_at, and deleted_at only if the internal response contract permits it; do not invent fields beyond the schema. If the runtime response contract excludes deleted records, apply the project's existing account visibility rules rather than exposing hidden records.

If the seller is not found, return a not-found error. If the authenticated seller tries to access another seller's record, return forbidden. Keep the endpoint read-only with no transaction required. Ensure the serializer masks authentication secrets and preserves nullable timestamps exactly as stored.

responseBody.description: Seller account details.

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of administrator accounts for platform governance and oversight.

This operation lets a super administrator browse the registered administrator roster in the shopping mall platform. The underlying administrator account records represent governance identities with email/password credentials, a role grade, and account security state. The list is intended for administrative management work such as identifying regular administrators, identifying super administrators, and reviewing who currently has platform-level authority.

Because administrator grade management belongs to the administrative domain, this endpoint is restricted to super administrators. Regular administrators must not use this operation to manage peers or inspect the full administrator roster beyond what their own workflows allow. The response is optimized for management screens and should provide summary-level information rather than full credential or session data.

Use this endpoint together with the administrator grade management workflow when a super administrator needs to promote or demote an administrator. After reviewing the roster here, the caller can use the dedicated grade change operation to apply the authority change. If the target administrator needs a deeper record of historical changes, the administrator grade history data should be accessed through its own governance-oriented operation rather than expanding this list response.

The result is paginated and suitable for searching and filtering within the administrative domain. It should return consistent ordering for repeated queries, handle empty result sets cleanly, and exclude any information that is not necessary for roster oversight or grade administration.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query shopping_mall_administrators with search, filtering, pagination, and stable sorting for roster management.

Support filtering by administrator grade, account status, and other governance-oriented attributes that exist on the administrator record. Apply text search against administrator identity fields such as email or displayable account identifiers if present in the schema. Use a deterministic sort order, defaulting to newest or most recently created administrators first if a creation timestamp exists; otherwise use a stable primary-key ordering.

Enforce authorization so only super administrators can access the list. Regular administrators must be rejected. Do not expose password hashes, reset tokens, session tokens, or other authentication secrets. Return a paginated summary DTO with only the fields necessary for administration screens.

If the underlying schema contains related grade-history or security-state fields, surface them only as summary values, not as nested collections. Keep the query read-only and avoid side effects. Handle empty pages, invalid pagination values, and invalid grade filters with standard validation errors.

responseBody.description: Paginated administrator roster summaries.

requestBody.description: Search, filter, pagination, and sorting criteria for the administrator roster.

operations.description:
Retrieve a single administrator account by its unique identifier.

This operation returns the platform governance record stored in the `shopping_mall_administrators` table, which is the canonical identity source for administrator accounts. The record includes the administrator's email address, grade, account status, and timestamp metadata used for administration and oversight.

Only administrator actors should access this endpoint. Regular administrators may use it when reviewing administrator accounts within the platform management area, and super administrators may use it when performing grade-related governance tasks. The response intentionally excludes authentication secrets such as the password hash, since those values are internal to account security and must not be exposed through read operations.

The `administratorId` path parameter must be a UUID and must correspond to the primary key of the target administrator row. If the identifier does not match an existing administrator record, the service should return a not-found response. The endpoint does not modify data, does not require a request body, and is meant to be used alongside administrator request review and administrator grade management workflows when the UI needs to inspect a specific administrator account.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Load a single row from `shopping_mall_administrators` by primary key `id`.
Validate the `administratorId` path value as a UUID before querying.
Use a direct primary-key lookup; no joins are required for the base response.
Map the row to a read DTO that excludes `password_hash` and any internal-only security material.
Include `id`, `email`, `grade`, `account_status`, `created_at`, and `updated_at` in the response shape.
If the row is not found, return a 404-style domain error.
If the caller is not an administrator, deny access according to the platform's admin authorization rules.
Do not expose `deleted_at` in the public response unless the broader API design explicitly models account-deletion history for administrators; this endpoint should remain a standard detail lookup.

responseBody.description: Administrator account details.

operations.description:
Retrieve the authenticated customer's saved product list as a paginated wishlist view.

This endpoint returns the customer's personal shopping space for products they want to keep for later reference. A wishlist is a customer-owned collection that stores products rather than specific variants, so every item in the response represents interest in the product as a whole instead of a purchase-ready selection. The response is intended for customer-facing browsing, comparison, and later recall of saved products.

The wishlist data is built from the customer-owned wishlist entry table and joined with the current product records so the client can display product-level details in a coherent list. Because the product catalog is the source of truth for active listings, deleted products are not shown here; the list must remain coherent and only include products that still exist in an active state. The operation should preserve the business rule that wishlist membership is separate from cart contents and order history.

Only authenticated customers may use this endpoint because the collection belongs to the customer account. The returned page should support standard browsing controls such as pagination, keyword search, and sorting so customers can efficiently review their saved products. The list should be suitable for the wishlist screen where customers may inspect saved items, revisit product details, and manage their personal shopping preferences.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query the authenticated customer's wishlist entries from shopping_mall_wishlists using the customer identity from the access token or session context.

Join each wishlist row to shopping_mall_products to load current product data for display. Filter out records whose related product is no longer active, because deleted products must not appear in wishlist views. Keep the response strictly product-level; do not expose or accept variant-level wishlist data.

Support pagination, search, and sorting through the request body. Search should apply to product name and other list-facing product fields exposed by the product table. Sorting should default to newest saved first unless the request specifies a different supported order. Return a paginated container of wishlist summaries with enough product information for list rendering, not the full product detail payload.

Use a read-only transaction or equivalent consistent snapshot read to avoid partial visibility while products are being removed from wishlists by background cleanup. If the customer has no wishlist items, return an empty page rather than an error. If the request includes unsupported filters or invalid paging values, fail validation before querying. Authorization must reject non-customer callers.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of the customer's wishlist product summaries.

requestBody.description: Search, filter, pagination, and sorting criteria for the customer's wishlist.

operations.description:
Retrieve a single wishlist and its saved products for the authenticated customer.

A wishlist is a customer-owned collection of saved products that the customer wants to keep for later browsing and comparison. This operation returns the full wishlist resource identified by the wishlist ID, including the product-level saved items that belong to that wishlist. The response is intended for the customer’s personal shopping space and must reflect the business rule that wishlists store products rather than product variants.

Only registered customers can access wishlist data, and the request must be authorized against the wishlist owner. If the wishlist belongs to another customer, the request must be rejected. Administrative users may also access this resource for support or moderation purposes when permitted by the authorization layer. If a saved product was removed from the platform, it must not appear as an active wishlist item in the returned data.

This endpoint supports the wishlist browsing flow used together with the wishlist listing operation. The list view is paginated for browsing multiple saved products, while this detail view is used when the client needs the complete state of one wishlist. The returned structure should preserve the customer’s saved-product collection in a way that remains consistent with product deletions and other platform maintenance rules.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Load the wishlist row by wishlistId from shopping_mall_wishlists.
Verify the authenticated actor is a registered customer and that the wishlist belongs to that customer, unless the actor is an administrator with permission to inspect customer-owned shopping data.
If the wishlist does not exist, return a not-found error.
If ownership does not match, return a forbidden error.

Fetch the saved product entries associated with the wishlist using the wishlist's product-level relations. Do not expose any variant-level wishlist data, because wishlists are product-only by business rule.
If any referenced product no longer exists or is no longer active, exclude it from the active item set so the response does not surface deleted products as wishlisted items.

Return a single wishlist detail object that includes the wishlist identity and the current active saved products. The endpoint is read-only and must not modify wishlist contents, product state, or customer data.

responseBody.description: Wishlist details with the current saved products.

operations.description:
Retrieve the authenticated customer's active cart view, including its current line items and calculated totals.

This operation returns the customer's pre-order basket as a shopping cart resource collection, including the selected product-variant lines, their quantities, and the subtotal for each line. It is designed for cart review before checkout, so the response should always reflect the latest combined quantity for each selected variant and the current total price derived from all items in the cart.

The cart belongs to a customer account and represents the customer's current shopping state before an order is placed. When the same product variant is added more than once through other cart operations, the platform combines the quantities into the existing cart item rather than creating duplicate lines. This endpoint therefore exposes the consolidated cart view that results from those cart item rules.

Access to this endpoint is limited to the authenticated customer who owns the cart. The returned data is used together with checkout operations, shipping address selection, and payment confirmation flows. If cart contents have changed since the last view, the response must show the current item subtotals and cart total price so the customer can make an accurate purchase decision.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Read the active cart for the authenticated customer from shopping_mall_carts, including the cart's related shopping_mall_cart_items records and each item's associated product variant context.

Load the cart by the customer identity from the access token/session context. Enforce one-cart-per-customer behavior by selecting the customer's active cart record only. Join or hydrate the cart items in display order, and for each item calculate the live subtotal from the stored quantity and the current cart pricing rules. Return the cart total as the sum of all visible item subtotals.

Do not create, mutate, or delete any records in this operation. This endpoint is a read operation only, even though it uses PATCH because the interface requires request-body-driven retrieval patterns for more complex reads. If the cart does not exist yet for the authenticated customer, return the appropriate empty-cart representation if the application supports lazy cart creation; otherwise return not found according to the service convention.

Ensure the response reflects merged quantities for duplicate variant selections and the latest recalculated totals after any add, remove, or quantity-change action performed by other cart endpoints. Hide any implementation detail that would expose internal calculation artifacts; the API should present the customer-facing cart state only. Reject access when the authenticated principal does not own the cart being resolved.

responseBody.description: Paginated shopping cart view with items and calculated totals.

requestBody.description: Optional cart retrieval context for the current customer session.

operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of order items.

This endpoint returns purchased product-variant line items from the shopping mall order domain, including the item-level fulfillment state, purchased quantity, and the timestamps that describe how the line moved through shipping, delivery, cancellation, or refund workflows. It is designed for browsing many records at once, not for editing a single item, and it follows the platform rule that each order item keeps its own lifecycle history independently of the overall order.

The response is intended for customers reviewing their purchase history, sellers reviewing fulfillment work for their own products, and administrators performing platform oversight. Because the order item table is indexed by order, product variant, status, and creation time, this endpoint should support status-based filtering, time-based sorting, and pagination so large order histories can be searched efficiently.

The returned list must preserve the business meaning of each line item: quantity represents the number of units covered by that item, status reflects the item-level state only, and shipped, delivered, cancelled, and refunded timestamps must be treated as the authoritative lifecycle markers for the line. Related order, shipment, and snapshot data may be used by downstream detail views, but this endpoint should remain focused on searchable item summaries.

When used by a customer, the service must restrict results to items belonging to that customer’s orders. When used by a seller, the service must restrict results to order items for that seller’s products. When used by an administrator, the service may return all order items subject to the requested filters and paging rules. If a client needs a single item’s full detail, it should call the corresponding item detail endpoint rather than expanding this list response.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Implement a paginated order-item search query over shopping_mall_order_items with optional joins to shopping_mall_orders and shopping_mall_shipments for context filtering.

Use a request-body driven query because clients need flexible filtering and sorting across multiple criteria. Support filtering by item status, parent order identifier or order number, seller scope through shipment or product-variant ownership, shipment presence, created date range, and pagination controls. The query should default to newest-first ordering by created_at, consistent with list browsing expectations.

Enforce access control at the service layer: customers may only see items belonging to their own orders; sellers may only see items for products they own; administrators may see all items. Apply these scope constraints before returning results, and reject any attempt to query unauthorized records. Preserve the item-level semantics from the domain rules: do not derive item status from the overall order status, and do not collapse multiple item states into a single order state.

Project the result as a compact summary DTO suitable for list rendering. Include the order item id, parent order reference, purchased quantity, item status, shipped_at, delivered_at, cancelled_at, refunded_at, created_at, and minimal parent context needed for browsing. If needed, join the related order for order number and placement time, and join the product variant relationship only for seller/customer-facing display fields that are part of the summary schema. Avoid loading snapshot tables here because snapshots are for historical detail and dispute review, not for list search.

Use the existing indexes on status and created_at to keep the query efficient. If the request includes invalid status values, negative pagination values, or an unsupported sort field, return validation errors before querying the database. For empty result sets, return an empty page with correct pagination metadata.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of order item summaries.

requestBody.description: Search, filtering, sorting, and pagination criteria for order items.

operations.description:
Create a new purchased order item record for a selected product variant and quantity.

This operation records one transactional line item in the shopping mall order system. It is used when the platform needs to persist a committed purchase line that belongs to an order and points to a specific product variant. The stored record keeps the purchased quantity and the current item lifecycle state so that later shipment, cancellation, refund, and review workflows can operate on the same item-level history.

The created item represents a single variant purchase, which aligns with the domain rule that repeated purchases of the same variant within one order should be represented as one combined order item with an increased quantity. The item also serves as the durable reference for fulfillment and after-sales processes, while preserved purchase-state details are handled by the dedicated snapshot tables in the data model.

Only authenticated customer members should normally create order items through the storefront purchase flow, because the item belongs to a customer's order history and is part of the checkout-to-fulfillment lifecycle. Administrative access may be used for oversight tooling if the service exposes such internal use, but the endpoint itself is intended to create a customer purchase line rather than a catalog or inventory record.

The server must validate that the referenced order exists, the selected product variant exists, and the requested quantity is valid for the purchase workflow. System-managed lifecycle fields such as shipped time, delivered time, cancelled time, refunded time, status transitions, creation timestamps, and update timestamps must be assigned by the application layer and not accepted from the client. If the variant is unavailable or the quantity cannot be accepted by the business rules, the request must fail before persisting the line item.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Implement this endpoint as a service-layer create flow for shopping_mall_order_items.

1. Validate the request body and authenticate the caller as an authorized customer-side actor for purchase creation.
2. Resolve the parent order by its ID, ensure it belongs to the caller when the operation is used in a customer checkout context, and ensure the order is in a state that still allows item creation.
3. Resolve the target shopping_mall_product_variant and verify that the variant exists, is not deleted, and can be purchased according to the current stock and item-state business rules.
4. Enforce quantity rules: quantity must be a positive integer, and the final order-line quantity should represent the combined purchased units for the chosen variant. If the same variant already exists in the order within the same transactional context, the application should merge the quantity rather than creating a duplicate item record.
5. Create the shopping_mall_order_items row inside a transaction together with any necessary downstream inventory or order-state side effects. The live schema includes shopping_mall_order_id, shopping_mall_product_variant_id, quantity, status, shipped_at, delivered_at, cancelled_at, refunded_at, created_at, updated_at, and deleted_at. Initialize status to the committed paid state and leave the lifecycle timestamps null until the corresponding workflow updates occur.
6. Do not accept client input for shipped_at, delivered_at, cancelled_at, refunded_at, created_at, updated_at, or deleted_at; these are system-controlled fields.
7. Return the newly created order-item entity after persistence. If the application layer performs order status recalculation, do it after the item insert within the same transaction so order history remains consistent.
8. Handle common failures with clear business errors: order not found, variant not found, invalid quantity, variant unavailable, order not eligible for item creation, or quantity merge conflicts when the same variant is being processed concurrently.

responseBody.description: Created order item record.

requestBody.description: Order item creation data including the target order, variant, and purchase quantity.

prerequisites.description: A product must exist before a purchasable variant can be created and referenced by the order-item workflow, so this creates the parent product resource needed for the selected variant.

A product variant must be created before it can be purchased in an order item, because the order item stores a variant reference and the purchase flow requires an existing purchasable variant resource.

operations.description:
Retrieve a single cart item owned by the authenticated customer.

This operation returns the complete cart-item record used in the shopping cart workflow, including the selected product variant, the quantity currently stored in the cart, and the pricing information needed to render the cart line and prepare checkout. In the shopping mall domain, a cart item represents one specific product-variant entry inside a customer's active cart, so the response is intended for cart detail screens and cart validation before purchase.

The cart item is part of the customer's private shopping state, so access must be limited to the owning customer, with administrative access only if the platform's authorization layer explicitly allows support or oversight access. If the requested cart item does not belong to the authenticated principal, the server must deny the request. If the cart item exists but the underlying product variant has changed or become unavailable, the operation should still return the stored cart item data so the client can present the current cart state accurately.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Load the cart item by cart_item_id and verify ownership against the authenticated customer.

Perform a primary lookup on shopping_mall_cart_items using the path identifier. Join or hydrate the related product variant context from shopping_mall_product_variants and shopping_mall_products as needed for the response payload, but do not recalculate business totals beyond the stored cart-item state unless the underlying cart rules require current pricing display. Enforce that the cart item belongs to the authenticated customer through the parent cart relationship before returning the record.

If the item is missing, return a not-found response. If ownership fails, return forbidden. If the item references a variant that is unavailable or deleted, keep the cart item readable and surface the related availability state through the response DTO so the client can warn the user. No transaction is required because this is a read-only detail operation.

responseBody.description: Detailed cart item information including the selected variant and quantity.

operations.description:
Update the quantity of a single cart item in the customer's active cart.

This endpoint modifies one stored cart line in the shopping basket that belongs to the authenticated customer. The cart item is the normalized child record that connects the owning cart with a selected product variant, and it stores the intended purchase quantity for that variant. The request does not reselect the cart or variant; it only updates the editable quantity on the existing item identified by `cartItemId`.

The service must confirm that the target cart item belongs to the current customer's cart before applying any change. It must also verify that the selected product variant still exists and is available for shopping, because cart item rows are only meaningful when the linked variant is still valid. Quantity changes should preserve the one-variant-per-line rule enforced by the cart model, so the implementation must update the existing row rather than create a duplicate row for the same variant.

If the requested quantity is invalid, missing, or conflicts with the current variant availability, the endpoint must reject the update and keep the cart unchanged. The response returns the updated cart item so the client can redraw the cart immediately after a successful edit.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Load the cart item by cartItemId with its owning cart and linked product variant. Confirm the cart belongs to the authenticated customer; otherwise return a not-found or forbidden-style error without revealing ownership details. Reject the request if the cart item is deleted.

Validate the incoming quantity in the request body as a positive integer. If the quantity is zero, negative, or exceeds business limits, return a validation error. If the linked variant is unavailable for purchase, reject the update. If the business layer enforces stock-aware cart limits, compare the requested quantity against the variant's current sellable quantity and return an error or warning according to service rules.

Apply the quantity update in a single transaction and persist the updated timestamp. Do not modify the cart identity, variant identity, or any product fields. Do not create a new cart item row because the schema already enforces one row per cart-variant combination through a unique constraint. After saving, return the refreshed cart item record for the client to update cart totals on the frontend.

responseBody.description: Updated cart item information.

requestBody.description: New quantity for the existing cart item.

operations.description:
Remove an item from the authenticated customer’s shopping cart.

This operation deletes a single cart line identified by the cart item ID. It is used when a customer decides that a specific product variant should no longer remain in the active cart before checkout. The cart item concept represents one variant entry inside a cart, including its quantity and subtotal meaning, so removing it changes the cart contents immediately and may affect the cart total shown to the customer.

Only the owning customer may perform this action. The server must verify that the cart item belongs to the current authenticated customer and is part of that customer’s active cart before removing it. If the item does not exist or does not belong to the caller, the request must be rejected. This endpoint does not modify products, variants, stock history, or order history; it only removes the selected cart entry from the current basket.

This operation is commonly used together with cart retrieval and cart update operations. After successful deletion, clients should refresh the cart state so that item totals and the overall cart total reflect the reduced contents.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Implement a cart-item deletion service that deletes one shopping cart line by cartItemId.

Lookup the cart item by its primary identifier and ensure it belongs to the current authenticated customer’s cart. If the record does not exist, or the cart is not owned by the caller, return a not-found or forbidden-style error according to the project’s error handling policy. The operation must not accept a request body.

Perform the delete in a transaction if the cart total is recalculated in the same flow. After removing the cart item, recalculate the parent cart’s totals and any summary fields used by the cart view so the UI receives an up-to-date cart state. Do not touch inventory records, product records, or order records.
